subject: Information Theory
title: Substitution Ciphers
description: Learn Substitution Ciphers in one minute.

hook.text: Replace each letter with a different letter: A becomes Q, B becomes X. The key space explodes to 26 factorial.

buildup.text: With 400 septillion possible keys, brute force is impossible. So substitution ciphers seem unbreakable.

discovery.text: Al-Kindi cracked them around 850 AD using frequency analysis. Letter patterns betray the substitution.

twist.text: English E appears roughly 13% of the time. The most common ciphertext letter is almost certainly E.

climax.text: A huge key space means nothing if the ciphertext leaks statistical patterns from the plaintext.

punchline.text: Big key space, leaky patterns. Size isn't everything.

quiz.question: How did Al-Kindi break substitution ciphers?
